claims.text: Rapid quenching will improve the glass-forming ability of phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys relative to slow cooling.
Rapid quenching will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to slow cooling.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 is a relevant phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy for the proposed intervention.
Melt-spinning can rapidly quench this alloy at approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s.
A short electric-arc pulse can provide accelerated cooling of this alloy.
The intervention should be applied under a controlled inert atmosphere.
A slow-cooling baseline of approximately 50 K/s is appropriate for comparison.
The intervention is expected to work in phosphorus-rich alloys with high mixing or configurational entropy.
Rapid quenching will produce a homogeneous amorphous structure.
The rapidly quenched amorphous structure will have reduced short-range order relative to the slowly cooled crystalline structure.
Slow cooling produces a complex multiphase crystalline microstructure.
Rapid quenching leaves insufficient time for atomic rearrangement.
The reduced time for atomic rearrangement suppresses crystalline-phase nucleation and growth.
Kinetic suppression of crystallization increases glass-forming ability.
Kinetic suppression during quenching delays crystallization during subsequent heating and thereby raises amorphous-state thermal stability.
Rapidly cooled samples will have more amorphous material than slowly cooled samples, as detectable by XRD and microscopy.
Rapidly cooled samples will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than slowly cooled samples.
Slow-cooled phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys have less thermally stable amorphous regions.
Increasing the diversity of micro-alloying elements at fixed total alloying content can reduce liquid fragility.
Different compositions or additional micro-alloying elements may alter the transformation kinetics and reduce the intervention's effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The electric-arc pulse is offered as an example of the rapid-cooling intervention, but the stated required range is 10^5–10^6 K/s, whereas the cited arc-pulse condition achieved only 3018 K/s. Melt-spinning, not the arc pulse, matches the specified range.
